tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Endpoints to retrieve account data using a data connection.

get.description:
Lists all connected accounts.

This API must be called using a `client_credentials` bearer token.

The endpoint returns a maximum of 50 items. Pagination will be supported in the future.

Items are ordered by `type` ascending, then `id` ascending.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Cursor used for pagination. Pass the `next_cursor` value from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.
Note: cursor-based pagination is not yet active; this parameter is accepted but has no effect in the initial release.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filters results by resource type. Valid values are `account` and `card`.

post.description:
Creates an asynchronous request to retrieve transactions for an account over a date range.

The request is processed asynchronously: a `202` response returns the request `id` (use this value as `{request_id}` when polling) and an initial `status` of `pending`. Poll for the result using the returned `id`.

Results are paginated and returned in a stable order: by `timestamp` descending, then `id` descending as a unique tie-breaker. Pass the `next_cursor` from a previous page as `cursor` to retrieve the next page; a null `next_cursor` means there are no further transactions.

This API must be called using a `client_credentials` bearer token.

Note: `from`/`to` applies to settled transactions. Returned pending transactions may have dates outside the requested range — behaviour varies by bank.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the account.

get.description:
Retrieves the result of a previously created transactions request.

The response `status` is one of:
  - `pending` — the request is still being processed; poll again.
  - `completed` — the result is available in `result`.
  - `failed` — the request could not be completed; see `failure_reason`.

This endpoint is idempotent and re-readable: repeated reads of the same `request_id` return the same pre-computed page.
To retrieve a different page, create a new request via `POST` with the `next_cursor` value, which returns a new `request_id`.

This API must be called using a `client_credentials` bearer token.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the account.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the transactions request, as returned when the request was created.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the connection.

post.description:
Sent to the webhook URI that you registered when:
- a connection is authorised.
- a connection fails.

Sent to the configured webhook URI when an async transactions request reaches a terminal state:
- The request completed successfully. Call `GET /v3/connected-accounts/{account_id}/transactions/requests/{request_id}` to retrieve the transactions.
- The request failed.

TlUserIpHeader.name: Tl-User-IP
TlUserIpHeader.description:
Used to collect and record the end-user's IP address.
The first IP address in the list will be used as the end-user IP address.
Necessary to overcome 4 calls per day rate limits.

DeviceUserAgentHeader.name: X-Device-User-Agent
DeviceUserAgentHeader.description:
Used to improve the end-user's authentication experience based on their device type.
If omitted, the `User-Agent` header will be used instead.
This header is only considered if the authorization_flow object in the request body is specified.

WebhookSignatureHeader.name: Tl-Signature
WebhookSignatureHeader.description:
A JWS with detached content, verifiable with our public key.
See [Webhook Request Signing](/docs/configure-webhooks-for-your-integration#validate-the-signature-of-received-webhooks)

AccountIdentifierScan.description: The scheme identifier for a bank account participating in UK payment schemes.

iban.description: Valid International Bank Account Number (no spaces). Consists of a 2 letter country code, followed by 2 check digits, and then by up to 30 alphanumeric characters (also known as the BBAN). pattern: `^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2}[A-Z0-9]{11,30}$`

AccountIdentifier.title: Account Identifier
AccountIdentifier.description: A unique scheme identifier for an external account.

bic.description: The Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the account.

account_holder_names.description: The names of the account holders. May be empty if not provided by the bank.

type.description: Identifies this item as a card. Additional card-specific fields (e.g. card_network, card_type, partial_card_number) will be added here when card support is introduced in a future release.

Enrichment.title: Enrichment
Enrichment.description:
Configures the enrichments to perform on the retrieved transactions.
Currently both must be true; individual enrichments are not yet supported.

transaction_category.description: When `true`, enrich transactions with a category assigned to the transaction.

merchant_name.description: When `true`, enrich transactions with the name of the company associated with the transaction.

from.description: The start of the date range (inclusive) for which to retrieve transactions, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: The end of the date range (inclusive) for which to retrieve transactions, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

cursor.description: Cursor used for pagination. Pass the `next_cursor` value from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results.

page_size.description:
The maximum number of transactions to return per page. Optional; if omitted, defaults to 50.
The server returns `min(500, requested)` items.

enrichment.description: Optional. When provided, requests that enrichment be performed on the retrieved transactions.

id.description: The unique identifier of the transactions request.

status.description: The transactions request is still being processed. Poll again to retrieve the result.

TransactionCategory.title: Transaction Category
TransactionCategory.description: The category assigned to the transaction.

category_code.description: The code identifying the category assigned to the transaction.

category_name.description: The human-readable name of the category assigned to the transaction.

TransactionEnrichment.title: Transaction Enrichment
TransactionEnrichment.description:
Enrichment data derived for the transaction. Present only when enrichment was
requested on the transactions request. Individual fields are only populated
when they could be determined.

merchant_name.description: The name of the company associated with the transaction.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the transaction, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: Original description of the transaction as reported by the provider.

amount_in_minor.description: The transaction value in the minor unit of the currency. Negative for debits.

status.description: Whether the transaction is still pending or has settled.

enrichment.description: Enrichment data for the transaction. Present only when enrichment was requested on the transactions request.

id.description: The unique identifier of the transactions request.

status.description: The transactions request completed successfully and the result is available.

result.description:
The pre-computed page of transactions for this request.
Transactions are returned in a stable order: by `timestamp` descending, then `id` descending as a unique tie-breaker.
The page is re-readable for the lifetime of the request: repeated reads of the same `id` return the same page.
To retrieve the next page, create a new request with the `next_cursor` value. A null `next_cursor` means there are no further transactions.

next_cursor.description: Cursor used to retrieve the next page of results. If null, there are no more items to retrieve.

TransactionsRequestFailureReason.description:
The reason the transactions request failed.
This list is non-exhaustive — integrators should handle unknown values gracefully.

Examples:
- `provider_error`

status.description: The transactions request failed and no result is available.

release_channel.description:

customer_segments.description: The customer segments that providers cater to that should be returned. By default, returns retail only.

provider_ids.description: IDs of providers to include in those returned.

excludes.description: Options to exclude providers included by the filters

ConnectionUserCreate.title: User
ConnectionUserCreate.description: Details of the end user who is consenting to data access. If you are using your own Payment Initiation Service Provider (PISP) licence, these fields are not required. Otherwise `name` and one of `email`/`phone` are required.

id.description: A unique identifier for the user. If you don’t provide this, TrueLayer generates a value in the response. You can use the same value for multiple connections to indicate a returning user.

name.description: This is the full first and last name of your end user (not initials).

email.description: The email address of your end user.

phone.description: The phone number of your end user in formats recommended by [ITU](https://www.itu.int/oth/T0202.aspx?parent=T0202). The country calling code must be included and prefixed with a `+`.

Metadata.description: Optional field for adding custom key-value data to a resource. This object can contain a maximum of 10 key-value pairs, each with a key with a maximum length of 40 characters and a non-null value with a maximum length of 500 characters.

UserConsentPrecaptured.title: Pre-captured user consent
UserConsentPrecaptured.description: Indicates that the user has already consented to the connection.

captured_at.description: Timestamp the user consent was collected, in the UTC timezone.

UserConsentRequestAuthorizationFlowCaptu.title: Authorization flow captured
UserConsentRequestAuthorizationFlowCaptu.description: Indicates that the user consent will be captured via the authorization flow.

HostedPageParametersResultPage.title: Result Page
HostedPageParametersResultPage.description: Parameters for hosted page when used to display result page after the provider authentication.

language_code.description:
The language code of the user. This is used to determine which language to show on the hosted page, overriding the browser's locale.
The language code must be in ISO 639-1 format.

HostedPageParametersAuthorizationFlow.title: Authorization Flow
HostedPageParametersAuthorizationFlow.description:
Parameters for hosted page when used in the authorization flow. Set this to receive an automatically constructed hosted page URI in the response. 
This cannot be provided if the root-level authorization_flow parameter is also set.

return_uri.description:
The URI where the user will be redirected to after the authorization flow has completed on the hosted page.
You must register the `return_uri` in your [settings in Console](/docs/app-settings#allowed-redirect-uris).

country_code.description:
The country code of the user. This is used to determine which banks to show on the hosted page initially.
The country code must be in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format.

language_code.description:
The language code of the user. This is used to determine which language to show on the hosted page, overriding the browser's locale.
The language code must be in ISO 639-1 format.

HostedPageParameters.title: Hosted Page Parameters
HostedPageParameters.description: Configuration parameters for TrueLayer's hosted page(s), which are displayed to the user during the authorization journey. The type determines which parts of the flow TrueLayer handles.

ReturnUri.description:
During the flow, the end user authorises the connection on a third-party site, such as a bank. The return_uri you set is where the user is redirected to after they complete authorisation on the third-party site. 

You must register the return_uri in your [settings in Console](/docs/app-settings#allowed-redirect-uris).

AuthorizationFlowRequest.title: Authorization flow
AuthorizationFlowRequest.description:
This object contains a declaration of your UI's capabilities.
You cannot provide this if also using the hosted_page option with type=authorization_flow.

redirect.title: Redirect
redirect.description:
Can your UI redirect the user to a third-party page?
For most providers, the user authorises the connection after they're redirected to their chosen provider's page. There, they can sign in with their credentials and approve the data access. This parameter states whether your UI can handle such a redirect.

DataAccessType.title: Data access type
DataAccessType.description:
Determines how long access to the end user's bank data is maintained after the initial authorisation.
- `one_time` — Data can only be retrieved within a single access window immediately after the user authorises with the bank. No further access is possible without a new connection.
- `recurring` — Data can be retrieved repeatedly throughout the full consent window, even when the user is not actively logged in or present, without requiring the user to re-authorise with bank each time.

scopes.description: The list of scopes that the user consents to. The Data Access endpoints return data only for the scopes that you request.

HostedPage.title: Hosted Page
HostedPage.description: Returned if the `hosted_page` object in the request body is populated.

uri.description: The URI to redirect the user to to authorize the connection using the hosted page.
URL the end user must be redirected to.

ActionSpecProviderSelection.title: Provider Selection
ActionSpecProviderSelection.description: Provider selection represents the end user's action of selecting a provider

providers.description: List of providers to be presented to the end user.

user_recommended_provider_ids.description:
List of recommended providers for the user, in order of most to least recommended.
Note that this is only populated if `user_recommended_provider_ids` is set to `true` when starting the authorization flow, and TrueLayer has recommendations for the user.

event_version.description: The version of the event schema.
